Findings describe documented vendor behavior or accessibility guidance, not Whiteboard capabilities, school requirements, usability measurements or integration readiness.

Local source basis

Read CLAUDE.md, NOTES.md, HANDOFF.md, design/README.md, the academic scope review, decisions D17–D38 and D59–D65, relevant batch02 authoring/file/rubric sources, batch03 grader/gradebook/release sources, batch04 people/copy/insights sources, and canonical app-map screen/route data. These establish the existing distinctions and historical concepts. They do not authorize changing legacy IDs or claiming that planned controls are production services.

  • design/reviews/academic-scope-review-2026-11-04.md: grading-policy/student-grade gaps, group-work completeness, grading-task calendar, optional achievements/assistant, and no direct messaging.
  • design/decisions.md: graded versus released; immutable receipt/release history; scoped TAs; instructor-owned release, allowances and score-affecting rubric application; no private medical records; future-only copy.
  • design/batch02/screens_teach_a.js, screens_teach_b.js: S14–S16/P47–P49 authoring, validation, preview, resource versions and in-use rubric proposals.
  • design/batch03/screens_grade.js: S17–S20 question-specific grading, manual override preservation, dual staff/learner calculations and exact stale-preview blocking.
  • design/batch04/screens_course.js: S21–S23 expiry/revocation, operational allowances, excluded copy activity and source-backed attendance.
  • handoff/academic-webapp-2026-11-04/spec/02_NAVIGATION_AND_PERMISSIONS.md, 04_WORKFLOWS_AND_RECORDS.md, 06_DECISIONS_AND_TRACEABILITY.md: proposed WD defaults, initial quiz types, fixture policy and conservative TA defaults.

Interpretation and unresolved decisions

W35–W60 are new proposed web route templates, not claims that standalone routes already exist. S/P IDs remain legacy references. W36/W37, W42, W47, W52, W54, W55–W57 and W60 make academic workflows explicit without editing the old atlas or D61/D62. W60 is course-content transfer only; no institution administration or live grade integration is included.

The main fixture uses Assignments 40%, Labs 25%, Quizzes 35%. Aisha's released calculation is 84.50%; held PS4 changes staff calculation to 85.17%. The coworker 10/25/25/40 setup is a separate configurable validation scenario. First HTML supports points and weighted calculations, four quiz response types, two-decimal final display rounding, and no custom formulas or extra credit. Empty categories renormalise active weights provisionally; all-empty denominators produce no calculable grade.

Before production, confirm institutional grading/letter/late policies, exact timer expiry adjudication, archive retention, self-enrollment rules, post-submission group membership access, moderation rights, upload bounds and accessibility support. These open decisions do not prevent a labelled local HTML demonstration using the documented defaults.

O01–O03 are optional specifications only: no automatic adoption, UI enablement, inference provider, paid service or award engine. Their sources are the local academic review; no new external claim about badges or assistant quality is made.

Verification

The staff catalogue is an array of exactly W35–W60 plus O01–O03, with the requested per-page fields. Checks cover JSON parsing, ID uniqueness, schema shape, 4+ states and 3+ acceptance cases per page, allowed roles, permission boundaries and page-reference format. This is specification/source validation only; no production operation, browser acceptance, accessibility certification, commit, push or deployment was performed.
